root_idea.summary: The root centers on treating something as beneath regard: holding it cheap, lightly esteemed, or contemptible.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop branches of blaming and finding fault, undervaluing or despising, and specialized derived uses for reprovers and contemptuous persons. The Quranic Form VIII use realizes the branch of esteeming people lightly or regarding them as insignificant.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form rather than the attested imperfect form.

senses.definition: To regard someone as insignificant or of little account; to esteem lightly and despise.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction تَزْدَرِي أَعْيُنُكُمْ, the subject “your eyes” regards the people as few, insignificant, or beneath regard. The construction expresses esteeming them lightly rather than merely seeing them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To blame, find fault with, reprove, or reproach someone or his deed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reproach may be angry or severe, and the expression can also describe anger toward someone arising from friendly concern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mock, scoff at, deride, or ridicule someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as a further use of the Form I construction زَرَى عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hold a person, thing, case, or affair in little, light, or mean estimation; to contemn or despise it; or to lower its estimation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV construction is used with بِـ. It may also convey falling short of the estimation due to someone or something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring against someone an imputation of fault, vice, or a compromising matter, seeking to involve him in confusion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The imputed matter may be a fault, vice, thing, affair, or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who makes no account of someone and disapproves his conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This expression is associated with blaming, finding fault, displeasure, or reproving a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a skin used for water or milk: middling in size, between small and large.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use applied to a water- or milk-skin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who blames or finds fault with people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agentive noun for a person characterized by this conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contemning or despising; regarding others as beneath regard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial or adjectival use; the related form مُسْتَزْرٍ is also recorded.
A rare substantivized designation recorded as a further use of this word.

cautions: The Quranic form is attested once as the active imperfect تَزْدَرِي; the public headword is normalized to the Form VIII perfect اِزْدَرَى.
The Form VIII lexical entry in the supplied classical evidence is cross-referential; the explicit Quran-specific explanation is therefore grounded in the Quran-focused lexical evidence.

A classical parenthetical leaves unclear whether the final gloss concerning making someone despised applies to أَزْرَى بِهِ, اِزْدَرَاهُ, or both; it has not been used to expand the Quranic sense beyond the directly supported use.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The supplied classical discussion does not resolve whether the gloss “made him to be contemned or despised” belongs specifically to أَزْرَى بِهِ or also to اِزْدَرَاهُ; the ambiguity is retained under the Form IV classical entry and does not alter the Quranic sense assignment.
